bands.blurb: Providers we have not scored yet — unknown, not zero.

providers.name: Accel
providers.description: Accel is one of the world's leading venture capital firms, founded in 1983 by Arthur Patterson and Jim Swartz and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with additional offices in San Francisco, London, and Bangalore, India. Accel describes itself as "the first partner to exceptional teams everywhere," backing founders from seed and early stage through growth worldwide. The firm invests across enterprise software and SaaS, consumer, artificial intelligence, fintech, cybersecurity, infrastructure and developer tools, security, media, and healthcare, and operates dedicated funds for the US, Europe/Israel, and India/Southeast Asia. Accel is known for its "prepared mind" investment philosophy and for backing category-defining companies including Facebook, Slack, Dropbox, Atlassian, CrowdStrike, UiPath, Qualtrics, Spotify, Flipkart, Swiggy, Freshworks, 1Password, Vercel, Scale AI, Anthropic, and Perplexity. Its portfolio spans more than 100 unicorns, dozens of IPOs, and hundreds of acquisitions. In 2024 Accel raised a $650M fund for European and Israeli startups, and in 2025 raised a fund for India and Southeast Asia. This profile tracks Accel's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Battery Ventures
providers.description: Battery Ventures is a global, technology-focused investment firm founded in 1983 and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, with additional offices in San Francisco, Menlo Park, New York, London, and Tel Aviv. Battery invests across every stage of a company's life, from seed and early-stage venture through growth equity and private-equity buyouts, giving the firm a distinctive multi-stage perspective on technology markets. Its core areas of focus are application software, infrastructure software, consumer technology, and industrial tech plus life-science tools. As of 2025 the firm reports having invested in more than 530 companies over its 40-plus-year history, of which roughly 70 have gone public and another 185 have been merged or acquired. Battery is currently investing out of its 15th flagship fund, Battery Ventures XV, capitalized at $3.25 billion, and has raised more than $16 billion across all of its funds since inception. The firm describes itself as decisive, hard-working, and thesis-driven, backing category-defining companies including Affirm, Amplitude, AppDynamics, Avalara, Akamai, Coupa, Wonolo, and many others. This profile tracks Battery Ventures' identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Benchmark
providers.description: Benchmark is an American early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1995 by Bob Kagle, Bruce Dunlevie, Andy Rachleff, Kevin Harvey, and Val Vaden, and headquartered at 140 New Montgomery Street in San Francisco, California (with a second office in Woodside). Benchmark is known for its distinctive equal partnership structure, where a small number of general partners share ownership and carry equally with no junior/senior hierarchy and no managing partner. The firm concentrates on leading first institutional rounds — typically Series A — and historically kept fund sizes small (around $425M) with a focus on consumer, marketplaces, social, open source, developer tools, infrastructure, enterprise software, fintech, crypto, and artificial intelligence. Benchmark has backed transformational companies including eBay, Uber, Twitter, Instagram, Snap, Dropbox, Discord, Docker, Zendesk, Confluent, Elastic, New Relic, Asana, Amplitude, Nextdoor, Stitch Fix, Yelp, OpenTable, Zillow, Red Hat, Airtable, Benchling, Cockroach Labs, Chainalysis, HackerOne, Contentful, Modern Treasury, Stytch, and, more recently, AI-native companies such as LangChain, Cerebras, MindsDB, Lovable, Legora, Gumloop, and Starcloud. In 2026 Benchmark broke with tradition to raise roughly $2B across two new vehicles, including its first-ever dedicated later-stage growth fund. This profile tracks Benchmark's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bessemer Venture Partners
providers.description: Bessemer Venture Partners (BVP) is one of the oldest and largest venture capital firms in the world, founded in 1911 out of the fortune of steel magnate Henry Phipps and headquartered in San Francisco, California. With more than $20 billion in assets under management and investment teams in San Francisco, Silicon Valley, New York, Boston, London, Bangalore, and Tel Aviv, Bessemer invests globally across seed, early, and growth stages, and runs a dedicated private equity buyout arm, BVP Forge. The firm invests across artificial intelligence and machine learning, cloud and infrastructure, developer tools, cybersecurity, fintech, healthcare and biotech, consumer, marketplaces, vertical software, data, deep tech and defense, and crypto/web3. Bessemer has backed transformative companies including Shopify, Twilio, Pinterest, LinkedIn, Yelp, DocuSign, Wix, Fiverr, Toast, ServiceTitan, PagerDuty, Auth0, Box, and Canva, and is known for publishing its "Anti- Portfolio" of missed opportunities, its Atlas research roadmaps, and its cloud/state-of-the-industry benchmark reports. Investing out of its 12th early-stage fund (a $3.85B vehicle), Bessemer was ranked among the largest venture firms by five-year fundraising. This profile tracks Bessemer's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cowboy Ventures
providers.description: Cowboy Ventures is a seed-stage venture capital firm founded in 2012 by Aileen Lee (who coined the term "unicorn" for billion-dollar startups) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. The firm backs pre-seed and seed-stage founders building "life-changing" products for large and growing markets, with roughly 70% of investments made pre-product and a strong seed-to-Series A graduation rate. Typical first checks run from about $100K up to $1M, with a sweet spot near $500K–$800K. Cowboy invests across enterprise software, fintech, software infrastructure and security, healthcare, consumer, future of work, and vertical software, primarily in the United States. The firm has made 100+ early-stage investments and cultivates a curated community of founders, operators, and tech leaders. Notable portfolio companies include Chime, Guild, Drata, Dollar Shave Club, Ironclad, Aura, Kiavi, Crunchbase, and Product Hunt.

providers.name: Craft Ventures
providers.description: Craft Ventures is a San Francisco-based venture capital firm founded in late 2017 by repeat entrepreneurs David Sacks and Bill Lee, built "by founders for founders" and rooted in the operator playbook of the PayPal Mafia. The firm invests across early and growth stages, writing checks that range from micro-seed positions through double-digit millions, and specializes in B2B SaaS, marketplaces, and enterprise software prized for high-growth, high-margin, recurring-revenue economics. Craft is known for its rigorous, metrics-driven SaaS operating framework and hands-on support spanning talent, go-to-market, community, and finance. Beyond core SaaS, the portfolio spans artificial intelligence, developer tools, fintech and crypto, cybersecurity, digital health, defense, and frontier technology. The firm manages roughly $3.3 billion in assets across four early-stage funds and two growth funds, including Craft Ventures IV ($712M) and Craft Ventures Growth II ($608M). Notable investments include Airbnb, Affirm, Reddit, Uber, Lyft, Palantir, Slack, ElevenLabs, Supabase, Anduril, and Neuralink. Headquartered in San Francisco, with offices in New York City and Austin, Texas, and a primarily United States geographic focus.

providers.name: DCM Ventures
providers.description: DCM Ventures (formerly Doll Capital Management, and commonly known as DCM) is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1996 by Dixon Doll, a former Accel partner, and David Chao, and headquartered at 2420 Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park, California with additional offices in Beijing and Tokyo. DCM was among the first Silicon Valley firms to build a cross-border, US-Asia investing practice, and typically leads early-stage rounds with checks in the roughly $1M-$5M range, deploying capital into a small group of category-defining companies each year rather than investing broadly. The firm's thesis has evolved from its original focus on communications and semiconductors toward consumer internet and SaaS, and today centers on vertical SaaS, fintech, cross-border innovation, and AI-native applications across the United States, China, Japan, and Southeast Asia. As of 2025 DCM manages approximately $4.5 billion in assets and reports 400+ portfolio companies, 35+ unicorns, and over $150 billion in aggregate market value, with notable investments including SoFi, Bill.com, Kuaishou, Matterport, 51job, Careem, and Sansan.

providers.name: Founders Fund
providers.description: Founders Fund is a San Francisco-based venture capital firm founded in 2005 by Peter Thiel, Ken Howery, and Luke Nosek, best known for the credo "we wanted flying cars, instead we got 140 characters" and a contrarian appetite for hard science and frontier technology over incremental consumer apps. The firm backs category-defining, often monopoly-scale companies across aerospace and defense, artificial intelligence, biotech, fintech and crypto, energy, semiconductors, robotics, and deep tech, investing from seed through late-stage growth with an increasingly concentrated, high-conviction style (its recent growth funds put hundreds of millions of dollars into a small number of companies). Founders Fund manages roughly $17 billion in assets as of 2025 and is headquartered at the Letterman Digital Arts Center in San Francisco's Presidio. Its portfolio includes many of the defining technology companies of the era, among them SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril, Stripe, Airbnb, Facebook, Neuralink, OpenAI, DeepMind, Ramp, Nubank, Spotify, and Figma.

providers.name: GGV Capital
providers.description: GGV Capital (Granite Global Ventures) was a global, multi-stage venture capital firm founded in 2000 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with offices in San Francisco, Shanghai, Beijing, and Singapore. GGV invested from seed through growth stage across Social/Internet and consumer, Enterprise Tech and SaaS, and Smart Tech (fintech, infrastructure, developer tools, cybersecurity, AI, and cross-border commerce), with a distinctive US–Asia bridge thesis. At its peak the firm managed roughly $9.2B in assets under management and backed more than 400 companies, including 44 unicorns and dozens of IPOs — among them Airbnb, Slack, Square, Affirm, HashiCorp, Coinbase, Peloton, Opendoor, Poshmark, StockX, BigCommerce, Grab, Alibaba, ByteDance, Zendesk, and Xpeng. On March 29, 2024 GGV Capital ceased using the GGV brand and split into two independent successor firms amid US–China tensions: Notable Capital (US/international, led by Hans Tung and Glenn Solomon, ~$4.2B AUM) and Granite Asia (Asia, led by Jenny Lee and Jixun Foo, ~$5B AUM). The former ggvc.com companies surface now redirects to Notable Capital, which carries the US/international portfolio graph. This profile tracks GGV Capital's identity and portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Khosla Ventures
providers.description: Khosla Ventures is a Menlo Park, California venture capital firm founded in 2004 by Sun Microsystems co-founder Vinod Khosla. The firm backs bold, early, and impactful ventures, favoring contrarian deep-tech bets with world-class teams and a conviction-driven approach that deliberately accepts a high failure rate to capture transformative outcomes. Khosla invests across seed, early (Series A/B), and growth stages through its Seed Fund, Main Fund, and Opportunity (growth) Fund, writing checks that range from small seed positions to large growth rounds. Focus sectors span artificial intelligence, enterprise and consumer software, financial services and fintech, robotics and frontier/deep tech, aerospace and defense, climate and sustainability (clean energy, fusion, materials, agriculture), and digital health, medtech, diagnostics, and therapeutics. The firm manages roughly $16 billion in assets as of 2025 and is known for early investments in OpenAI, Stripe, Square/Block, DoorDash, Instacart, Affirm, Impossible Foods, GitLab, Okta, Rocket Lab, and QuantumScape. Headquarters are at 2128 Sand Hill Road, Menlo Park, CA, with a primarily United States geographic focus and select global investments.

providers.name: Multicoin Capital
providers.description: Multicoin Capital is a thesis-driven crypto investment firm founded in 2017 by Kyle Samani and Tushar Jain, investing in cryptocurrencies, tokens, and blockchain companies and protocols believed to be reshaping trillion-dollar markets. The firm runs a hybrid structure of a hedge fund (its multi-billion dollar Master Fund, investing in public markets, direct positions, and strategic sales) alongside several venture funds that back early-stage companies, with venture checks ranging from roughly $1M to $50M. Its Venture Fund III closed at $422 million in January 2022. Multicoin invests across open and decentralized finance (DeFi), blockchain infrastructure and Layer 1/Layer 2 protocols, decentralized physical infrastructure networks (DePIN), stablecoins and payments, real-world asset tokenization, wallets, identity, gaming, and crypto-native consumer applications, with a well-known concentration around the Solana ecosystem. The firm's phoenix logo symbolizes a new financial system rising from the ashes of the old one, reflecting its long-term, high-conviction approach to absolute returns across market cycles. Headquartered in Austin, Texas, Multicoin manages capital on behalf of family offices, foundations, endowments, and institutional investors. In February 2026 co-founder Kyle Samani stepped back from day-to-day management, with operations continuing under co-founder Tushar Jain and partner Brian Smith.

providers.name: New Enterprise Associates
providers.description: New Enterprise Associates (NEA) is one of the world's largest and longest-running venture capital firms, founded in 1977 by Dick Kramlich, Chuck Newhall, and Frank Bonsal. Headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with offices in Timonium (Maryland), New York, and London, NEA invests across the full company lifecycle — "from idea to IPO" — spanning seed, Series A, and later growth rounds. The firm has raised over $27 billion in committed capital (as of December 31, 2024) and organizes into specialized practice groups across two core sectors: technology (enterprise software, consumer, fintech, AI, infrastructure) and healthcare (biopharma, life sciences, digital health, and medical devices). NEA is known for an active, hands-on partnership model and long-term support of category-defining companies, with a portfolio that has produced many notable IPOs and acquisitions including Cloudflare, MongoDB, Robinhood, Coursera, Databricks, Plaid, and Tempus.

providers.name: Redpoint Ventures
providers.description: Redpoint Ventures is a Silicon Valley venture capital firm founded in 1999 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with additional offices in San Francisco and Los Angeles and a history of China-focused funds in Beijing and Shanghai. Redpoint is a multi-stage investor that backs founders from seed and early stage through growth, running dedicated early-stage and growth teams. The firm invests across enterprise software and SaaS, AI and AI infrastructure, cloud and data infrastructure, developer tools, cybersecurity, fintech, consumer internet, healthcare, crypto/web3, and marketplaces. Typical checks range from roughly $0.5M-$2M at seed and $2M-$8M at Series A up to $10M+ at growth stage. As of 2025 Redpoint managed about $4.5 billion in assets, and its partners have participated in 130+ IPOs and acquisitions including Netflix, Snowflake, Twilio, Pure Storage, Zendesk, Stripe, HashiCorp, and HomeAway. The firm launched its tenth flagship fund, a $650M vehicle, in 2025, and publishes the annual InfraRed report on the leading private cloud and infrastructure companies. This profile tracks Redpoint's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sequoia Capital
providers.description: Sequoia Capital is one of the world's leading venture capital firms, founded by Don Valentine in 1972 and headquartered at 2800 Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park, California. Sequoia partners with founders from idea to IPO and beyond, investing across seed, early, and growth stages, and has backed transformative companies including Apple, Google, Oracle, Cisco, NVIDIA, PayPal, YouTube, Airbnb, Stripe, WhatsApp, Instagram, DoorDash, Snowflake, and Reddit. Its stated mission is to "help the daring build legendary companies," with a current focus on artificial intelligence and AI agents, autonomous systems, fintech, developer tools and infrastructure, healthcare, and consumer technology. Following its 2024 restructuring, Sequoia operates primarily across the US and Europe, while its former India/SEA and China arms became the independent firms Peak XV Partners and HongShan. This profile tracks Sequoia's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Shasta Ventures
providers.description: Shasta Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2004 and based in Silicon Valley (Portola Valley / Menlo Park, on and around Sand Hill Road, California). Founded by Rob Coneybeer and Ravi Mohan (with Tod Francis and Jason Pressman among its long-tenured Managing Directors), the firm invests primarily at the Series A stage in United States technology startups, typically leading rounds and taking board seats. Shasta has roughly $1.3B under management across multiple funds (Fund II $250M, Fund III $265M, Fund IV $300M) and a 20-year track record. Its thesis centers on enterprise software / SaaS, cybersecurity, developer tools and infrastructure, data intelligence, camera / computer vision, and consumer subscription products, pairing capital with operational support (Shasta Elevate) for technical founders. Notable investments include Anaplan, Zuora, Nest, Nextdoor, Apptio, Eero, Sendbird, Tonal, Lattice, Highspot, SentinelOne and Turo, with 12 unicorns, multiple IPOs and dozens of acquisitions across its history.

providers.name: Sierra Ventures
providers.description: Sierra Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded by Peter Wendell in 1982 and headquartered in San Mateo, California, in the heart of Silicon Valley. The firm invests from inception through Series A in first-principles founders under the tagline "Conviction Before Consensus," writing checks of up to $5M at seed and up to $10M at Series A. Sierra's current investment thesis centers on the next wave of enterprise technology: Vertical AI (purpose-built AI for specific industries), Infrastructure AI, Frontier and Deep Tech, and Physical AI and Robotics, alongside a longstanding history in enterprise applications, digital health, SaaS, and security. Over its 40-plus-year history the firm has invested more than $2 billion across 13 early-stage funds, with its 13th fund closing in 2023 at $265 million, following Fund 12 at $215 million and Fund 11 at $170 million. Sierra reports 35 IPOs and hundreds of successful exits, having backed companies such as Elastic, Astronomer, Chronosphere, CourseHero, Q-CTRL, Spectro Cloud, Endor Labs, and Reflection AI. The firm is notable for its CXO Advisory Board of Fortune 1000 enterprise leaders who help portfolio companies land early customers. This profile tracks Sierra Ventures' identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: SV Angel
providers.description: SV Angel is a San Francisco-based venture capital firm founded in 2009 by Ron Conway, one of Silicon Valley's most prolific angel investors. The firm runs two vehicles: an early-stage Seed Fund that writes roughly $200k checks into pre-seed and seed rounds, and a later-stage Growth Fund that invests at Series B and beyond. SV Angel is a founder-first, high-conviction investor that deliberately does not lead rounds, takes no board seats, and writes smaller checks as part of a larger syndicate so it can act as a neutral "routing layer" and advocate for founders. It is famous for its "Inflection Point Approach" — showing up at critical moments around fundraising, M&A, and business development. The firm invests almost entirely in US-based, software-driven companies across consumer and enterprise, and its portfolio has produced dozens of unicorns and landmark outcomes including Google, Airbnb, Coinbase, Stripe, Slack, Instacart, DoorDash, Reddit, Pinterest, GitHub, Databricks, Anthropic, and OpenAI.

providers.name: Threshold Ventures
providers.description: Threshold Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm based in Menlo Park, California that backs founder-led technology companies at the threshold of breakout growth. Threshold is the 2019 rebrand of Draper Fisher Jurvetson (DFJ), the storied Sand Hill Road firm founded in 1985; managing partners Emily Melton and Josh Stein spun the venture practice into an independent, focused fund. Threshold pursues a high-conviction strategy, concentrating on a small number of Series A and Series B investments and partnering hands-on with founders for the long term, frequently holding board seats through IPO and beyond. The firm invests across enterprise software and SaaS, developer tools and infrastructure, fintech, digital health and healthcare, and AI. Its portfolio has produced 10 unicorns, 3 IPOs, and 17 acquisitions, and includes Box, Twilio, Redfin, Remitly, Doximity, Rippling, LaunchDarkly, Livongo, and Talkdesk. Threshold has invested in roughly 87 companies and raised a ~$250M fund following the rebrand.

providers.name: TOCA Football
providers.description: TOCA Football, Inc. is a technology-enabled soccer experience and entertainment company headquartered in Costa Mesa, California, founded on the training methodology of former US international and Premier League player Eddie Lewis. It operates two businesses: TOCA Soccer, a network of indoor soccer training centers across the United States, Canada and Mexico offering private training, classes, clinics, camps, youth and adult leagues, tournaments and pickup play; and TOCA Social, a soccer-themed dining and entertainment venue brand. Its training centers pair a proprietary ball-delivery machine and digitalized smart targets with the MyTOCA player app, which tracks session performance, player cards, leaderboards and progress. TOCA is the official soccer training partner of Major League Soccer. TOCA publishes no public API, SDK, webhook or developer program: its software ships only as end-user consumer apps and in-venue systems.

providers.name: Tory Burch
providers.description: Tory Burch LLC is an American luxury women's fashion label founded in February 2004 by designer Tory Burch and headquartered in New York City, trading under the legal entity River Light V, L.P. The privately held company designs and sells ready-to-wear clothing, designer shoes, handbags, small leather goods, jewellery, watches, eyewear, fragrance and beauty, swimwear and home decor, together with the Tory Sport activewear line, through roughly 400 boutiques worldwide, wholesale partners and a direct-to-consumer storefront at toryburch.com serving the United States, United Kingdom, the European Union and Asia. Its affiliated Tory Burch Foundation funds and educates women entrepreneurs. Tory Burch is a fashion and retail business rather than a software vendor: it operates no developer program, publishes no API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API contract, and holds no public GitHub organisation. Its storefront is a Next.js front end on Akamai over a Salesforce Commerce Cloud (Demandware) commerce platform with Adobe Scene7 media, and an Apigee API gateway fronts www.toryburch.com/api/ for first-party storefront traffic only, exposing no publicly registered proxy. The one machine-readable artifact the company does publish is a site-wide llms.txt.

providers.name: Trinity Ventures
providers.description: Trinity Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1986 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with more than three decades of history backing mission-driven entrepreneurs across technology and consumer markets. The firm takes a deliberately personal, low-capital-to-partner approach to early-stage investing, positioning itself as "the call you want to make, not the call you have to make" and emphasizing intellectual candor and lasting founder relationships. Trinity invests primarily at seed, Series A and Series B, with checks generally ranging from roughly $1 million to $15 million and averaging around $5 million. Its focus spans enterprise software and cloud infrastructure, developer tools, fintech, digital media and marketing technology, consumer products and services, healthcare, and artificial intelligence. Over nine funds the firm has managed on the order of $1.3 billion in assets and produced a track record that includes multiple unicorns, IPOs and roughly 130 acquisitions. Notable investments include Starbucks, New Relic, Auth0, Turo, Care.com, Zulily, Blue Nile, Aruba Networks, Infoblox, Cohesity, Outreach, InfluxData, Contentful and Docker. Trinity invests primarily in the United States.

providers.name: Uncork Capital
providers.description: Uncork Capital is a San Francisco-based seed-stage venture capital firm founded in 2004 by Jeff Clavier, who formalized his angel portfolio into one of Silicon Valley's earliest dedicated seed funds; it operated as SoftTech VC until rebranding to Uncork Capital in 2017. Led by managing partners Jeff Clavier and Andy McLoughlin, the firm invests at the seed stage with a "first to believe" conviction style, typically targeting 10-15% ownership and writing seed checks broadly in the $1.5M-$4M range across B2B applications and SaaS, developer tooling, infrastructure and security, consumer and marketplaces, frontier tech/hardware, and AI/ML. In May 2025 the firm closed $300M in fresh capital across Uncork VIII (a $225M seed fund) and Uncork Plus IV (a $75M growth fund), bringing it to roughly $1.2B in assets under management. Across 275+ investments and 100+ outcomes, its portfolio and exits include SendGrid, Fitbit, Poshmark, Postmates, Eventbrite, LaunchDarkly, Tailscale, Front, Shippo, ClassDojo, Groq, Human Interest, Carrot Fertility, and GPTZero.
